history.player: Don't make this difficult. Hand it over or things will get unpleasant.
history.npc: Unpleasant? Come on now, we're not animals. I said I'll get the key, just give me a moment to breathe. No need to bring out the storm clouds, friend.

history.player: Hey! We're all getting together for the harvest dinner tonight. You should come!
history.npc: A harvest dinner, you say? That sounds like a fine thing indeed, a good way to shake off the dust and share some cheer. I'll be there, count me in!

history.player: It'll be a great time — the whole town will be there. Music, food, dancing.
history.npc: Dancing, you say? That sounds like a proper good time. Music and good company, can't ask for much more than that, can you?

history.player: I have evidence that Mayor Fletcher has been embezzling from the town fund for months.
history.npc:
"Mayor Fletcher? Embezzling? Well now, that's a rum do. A bit of news that might stir the pot, wouldn't you say?"

history.player: I've seen the ledgers myself. The numbers don't lie. What do you think we should do?
history.npc: Numbers don't lie, eh? That's a heavy bit of truth you're carrying there. We'll have to think carefully about how to handle such a thing, won't we?

history.player: Excuse me — my child is very sick and I can't afford a doctor. Could you help?
history.npc: A sick child, eh? That's a hard road to walk. Of course, I'll see what I can do to help, no one should face that alone.

history.player: Anything you can spare would mean the world. She has a fever and it's getting worse.
history.npc: A fever, you say? Poor little mite. Don't you worry, I'll sort you out with what you need. We'll get that child looked after.

history.player: The morning shipment arrived two hours early. Can you process it before market opens?
history.npc: Two hours early, you say? Well, that's a bit of a rush, but we'll manage. Just get the goods to the usual spot, and I'll see to it myself.

history.player: There are twelve crates. Can you get started right away?
history.npc: Twelve crates, right you are. I'll get them sorted, no need for you to worry your head about it. Just point me where they need to go.

history.player: There's a strange animal loose in the town square. Nobody knows what it is.
It hasn't attacked anyone but people are frightened. Some say it's a bad omen.
